text: Brain herniation is a serious medical condition where brain tissue is displaced from its normal position due to increased intracranial pressure (ICP) [ 1 , 2 ]. This can happen in stroke patients when there is significant cerebral edema (swelling) or large space-occupying lesions in the brain [ 2 , 3 ]. Brain herniation is a life-threatening condition and can cause various neurological manifestations (e.g., alterations in consciousness, abnormal pupillary responses, cranial nerve abnormalities, motor deficits, etc.) [ 4 ], leading to a poor prognosis and increased mortality rate [ 5 – 11 ]. Thus, timely detection of brain herniation and immediate medical intervention are crucial in improving the chances of survival in acute stroke patients admitted to the neurological intensive care unit (Neuro-ICU).
source_label: Automated quantitative pupillometry as a predictor for transtentorial brain herniation in patients with malignant acute ischemic stroke
